data_as_of: Intraday quotes from Yahoo Finance v7/v1 (~9:25 a.m. CT Nov 13, ~55 minutes into the session), spot-checked against StockAnalysis.com quote API (~9:26 a.m. CT). VIX, Russell 2000 and 10Y quotes are ~15-min delayed (~9:09 a.m. CT). Prior closes are Thursday Nov 12.
headline: Chips slide again after Nvidia's CEO exit and a hot 6.5% y/y PPI print: Nasdaq-100 −2.2%, SOXX −5.5%, AMD −9.7%, 10Y at 5.15%, Bitcoin below $70K.
drivers: Stocks opened slightly higher but turned lower after October PPI: +0.3% m/m (below the 0.4% consensus) but +6.5% y/y, the biggest annual rise since 2022, with core at 4.9%. That reinforces pricing for a 25 bp Fed hike in December, and the 10-year yield hit ~5.16%, its highest since October. Chips are the epicenter again: Nvidia (−3.7%) is digesting Jensen Huang's resignation and new allegations of a third affair ahead of earnings next Tuesday, while AMD (−9.7%), Broadcom (−6.2%), Marvell (−8.7%), Applied Materials (−6.0%, post-earnings) and the AI-compute names (NBIS, CRWV, IREN, CIFR, APLD) fall harder. Cisco is −5.3% despite raising its AI outlook (margin pressure, Citi says growth may have peaked), and a Microsoft service outage is weighing on MSFT. Bitcoin dropped below $70K for the first time in nearly three months, pulling crypto miners and MSTR/COIN lower. Counter-moves: Modine +25% on a report that Samsung is eyeing a deal, Cerebras +7.6% on a guidance raise and hyperscaler deals, Nu +7.5% on record profit.

notes: Scheduled for 7:47 a.m. CT but the run started at 9:24 a.m. CT, after the open; session = REGULAR SESSION. All tables use intraday quotes vs Thursday's close, and the gap screen uses the intraday move instead of the pre-market gap.

The Mac browser worked: Yahoo Finance v1 screener (US, price ≥ $5, market cap ≥ $2B) and v7 quotes were live with Nov 13 ~9:25 a.m. CT timestamps; MOD, HTFL, NVDA, LFTO, NBIS, SOXL and AMD cross-checked on the StockAnalysis quote API (within ~0.3 pt).
Yahoo's screener returned some stale rows (e.g. AAON, IBRX, AIMD, ICMB, INLF sorted out of order with small moves); those were dropped and all figures re-pulled from v7 quotes.
Rel vol everywhere = session volume so far ÷ 3-month average daily volume, not adjusted for time of day, so early-session values understate the full-day pace.
Cash-close % for Thursday is computed from the Thursday close vs Wednesday's close in the Nov 12 brief.
Russell 2000, VIX and 10Y quotes are ~15 minutes delayed. Bitcoin change is Yahoo's 24-hour figure. Gold is COMEX front-month (GC=F).
Economic calendar: only the 7:30 a.m. PPI release was verified; other scheduled releases and Fed speakers for today were not checked.
Under-$5 lists: exchange-listed only (Nasdaq/NYSE/NYSE American), session volume ≥ 500K. Float and reverse-split history weren't checked; flags are best-effort.
No git commands were run; the Mac publish agent handles commit and push.
